proposals.before: When he was about to face the law, Emperor Gaozu received him in audience at Taihua Hall, sent a attendant to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him suicide at his home.
proposals.after: When he was about to face the law, Emperor Gaozu received him in audience at Taihua Hall, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him suicide at his home.
proposals.reason: English article error: 'a attendant' must be 'an attendant'.

proposals.before: Later Hongzhi took Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang.
proposals.after: Later Hongzhi took Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang, as his wife.
proposals.reason: Chinese 得劉氏 indicates taking her as wife; the literal omits the marital sense present in the idiomatic.

proposals.before: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as Empress Yuan's brother and privately enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin.
proposals.after: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as Empress Yuan's brother and in public and private enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin.
proposals.reason: 公私自同外戚 means both public and private assimilation to imperial-affine status; the idiomatic keeps only privately.

proposals.before: At first Hongzhi had pretended to be the Empress Yuan's brother and had privately enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin by marriage.
proposals.after: At first Hongzhi had pretended to be the Empress Yuan's brother and had in public and private treated himself as equal to the imperial affines.
proposals.reason: 公私自同外戚 is public-and-private self-equation with imperial affines, not merely private enjoyment of marriage-kin privileges.

proposals.before: Once Zun took office as governor his greed was unchecked; in appointing subordinates he accepted numerous bribes.
proposals.after: Once Zun took up the governorship his original intent was still unquelled; in selecting and summoning subordinate officials he accepted many bribes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 本意未弭 means his original intent/purpose was not quelled, not that 'greed was unchecked'; the idiomatic rendering invents 'greed'.

proposals.before: In Lingqiu the Luo clan of Sizu was a powerful household in a rugged stronghold; many fugitives sheltered with them and joined in banditry.
proposals.after: In Lingqiu, Luo Sizu's clan was a powerful and overweening household dwelling in a rugged stronghold; many fugitives sheltered with them and joined in banditry.
proposals.reason: 羅思祖 is the personal name Luo Sizu; 宗門 is his clan/household. 'Luo clan of Sizu' wrongly treats Sizu as a place.

proposals.before: In Lingqiu the Luo clan of Sizu was a powerful and wealthy household dwelling in narrow defiles; many fugitives lodged with them and joined in robbery.
proposals.after: In Lingqiu, Luo Sizu's clan gate/household was powerful and overflowing in wealth, dwelling in narrow defiles; many fugitives lodged with them and joined in robbery.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 羅思祖 is a person name, not 'Luo clan of Sizu'.

proposals.before: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director Zhao of the Imperial Carriage Office to reinvestigate.
proposals.after: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Office Zhao of Qinzhou to reinvestigate.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 秦州 from 駕部令趙秦州, losing the identifying place/name element preserved in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: He was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
proposals.after: He was impeached and dismissed by Palace Aide of the Censorate Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
proposals.reason: 御史中尉 is the Palace Aide of the Censorate, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat (尚書).

proposals.before: He was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
proposals.after: He was impeached and dismissed by Palace Aide of the Censorate Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
proposals.reason: 御史中尉 is the Palace Aide of the Censorate, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat (尚書).

proposals.before: At first, through the xiucai examination he rose step by step to Governor of Southern Yanzhou; he misappropriated official roof tiles, his corruption was flagrant, and he was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Ping.
proposals.after: At first, through the xiucai examination he rose step by step to Governor of Southern Yanzhou; he misappropriated official roof tiles, his corruption was flagrant, and he was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Censors Li Ping.
proposals.reason: 御史中尉 is the censorial director (Yushi Zhongwei), not an office of the Imperial Secretariat (尚书).

proposals.before: He was posthumously granted the title Duke of the Secretariat and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title of Situ-gong and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
proposals.reason: 司徒公 is the honorary Three Dukes title Situ, not 'Duke of the Secretariat'.

proposals.before: He was posthumously granted Duke of the Secretariat and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted Situ-gong and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
proposals.reason: 司徒公 is Situ (Minister of Education / one of the Three Dukes), not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; she was later enfeoffed as Princess Chang of Xiangcheng, and Zan was therefore posthumously granted the title Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.after: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; she was later enfeoffed as Senior Princess of Xiangcheng, and Zan was therefore posthumously granted the title Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: 長公主 is the rank 'Senior/Grand Princess', not a personal name 'Chang'.

proposals.before: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; later she was enfeoffed as Princess Chang of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.after: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; later she was enfeoffed as Senior Princess of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: 長公主 denotes the senior-princess rank, not the given name Chang.

proposals.before: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.after: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Censors.
proposals.reason: 御史中尉 is the censorial director, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

proposals.before: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.after: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Censors.
proposals.reason: 御史中尉 is Yushi Zhongwei (censorial), not a Secretariat directorship.

proposals.before: Thus this scroll cannot be Wei Shou's original text; it was likely supplemented from works such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan, and the collation note at the end was accidentally lost.
proposals.after: Thus this scroll cannot be the original text of the Book of Wei; it was likely supplemented from works such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan, and the collation note at the end was accidentally lost.
proposals.reason: Chinese 魏書原文 means the original text of the Book of Wei, not specifically Wei Shou as person; the literal English already renders this correctly.

proposals.before: He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works. Commentary: The Minister of Works had no office titled 'ling.'
proposals.after: He served as Chief Clerk bearing the Support-the-State title under the Minister of Works (with a 'ling' in the wording). Commentary: The Minister of Works had no office titled 'ling.'
proposals.reason: Chinese 司空令輔國長史 is the office string under discussion; reading 輔國 as a separate 'Army' overcommits beyond the Chinese and the next note's clarification.

proposals.before: The character 'ling' is probably a superfluous addition; the meaning is that he served as Chief Clerk of the Secretariat to the Minister of Works with the rank of General Who Supports the State.
proposals.after: The character 'ling' is probably a superfluous addition; the meaning is that he served as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works with the rank of General Who Supports the State.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司空長史 is Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works; the literal English invents 'of the Secretariat,' which is absent from the Chinese.

decisions.reason: Before the vowel sound of attendant, English requires an, not a; the Chinese 遣侍臣 is unchanged and the proposed wording is otherwise identical.
得劉氏 in this marital context means taking Lady Liu as wife; s0062–s0063 call her one of the two wives (二妻). The literal omitted that sense; adding as his wife restores it.
公私自同外戚 requires both public and private assimilation to imperial-affine status; the idiomatic's privately alone drops 公.
公私自同外戚 is self-equation with the imperial affines in public and private, not merely privately enjoying marriage-kin privileges; the proposed literal restores 公私 and 自同.
本意未弭 means his original intent was not quelled; rendering it as greed was unchecked invents greed absent from the Chinese of this unit.
羅思祖 is the personal name Luo Sizu (cf. s0136 思祖家黨); 宗門 is his clan. Luo clan of Sizu wrongly treats Sizu as a place.

decisions.after: In Lingqiu, Luo Sizu's clan was a powerful and overflowing household dwelling in narrow defiles; many fugitives lodged with them and joined in robbery.
decisions.reason: 羅思祖 is a personal name, so Luo clan of Sizu is wrong; but the proposed clan gate/household is awkward scholarly gloss. Revise to natural Luo Sizu's clan while keeping 豪溢 as powerful and overflowing.
駕部令趙秦州 includes 秦州 as the identifying name/place element; the idiomatic's bare Director Zhao omits it.
御史中尉 is the Palace Aide of the Censorate, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat (尚書).
The literal likewise misrenders 御史中尉 as Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Palace Aide of the Censorate is the correct office.
御史中尉李平 holds the censorial directorship, not an Imperial Secretariat office; Director of the Imperial Censors matches the Chinese.

decisions.after: He was posthumously granted the title of Duke Situ and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
decisions.reason: 司徒公 is the Three Dukes honor Situ, not Duke of the Secretariat; but bare Situ-gong is awkward in running English. Duke Situ restores the office correctly and reads naturally.

decisions.after: He was posthumously granted Duke Situ and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
decisions.reason: Same office error as the idiomatic: 司徒公 is Situ, not the Secretariat; revise Situ-gong to natural Duke Situ.
襄城長公主 uses 長公主 as the senior-princess rank, not a personal name Chang; Senior Princess of Xiangcheng is correct.
The literal likewise misreads 長公主 as Princess Chang; Senior Princess of Xiangcheng restores the rank title.
除安南將軍、御史中尉 appoints him Yushi Zhongwei (censorial director), not Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
The literal has the same Secretariat misreading of 御史中尉; Director of the Imperial Censors is required.
魏書原文 means the original text of the Book of Wei, not Wei Shou's personal original; the proposed idiomatic matches the Chinese and the unit's literal.

decisions.after: He served as Chief Clerk with the Support-the-State title under the Minister of Works, the wording including 'ling.' Commentary: The Minister of Works had no office titled 'ling.'
decisions.reason: Reading 輔國 as a separate Army overcommits beyond 司空令輔國長史; the proposal rightly drops Army but remains awkward. Revise to natural English that keeps Support-the-State as title and flags the problematic ling.
意謂以輔國將軍為司空長史 is Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works; of the Secretariat is invented and absent from the Chinese.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0014 shows Princess Chang came only from misreading 長公主 as a given name; the title claim must read Senior Princess of Xiangcheng.
Accepted r0014 likewise shows the noble-title English Princess Chang is an artifact of the bad translation; revise to Senior Princess of Xiangcheng.
